verified_against: hyprlock (hyprwm) manual at hyprland-wiki main, fetched 2026-11-09
_note: Everything a generator may put into ~/.config/hypr/hyprlock.conf, recorded with its documented type and default. hyprlock is *forgiving*: an unknown variable is a warning and the lock screen still appears, so a typo silently ships a setting that does nothing. iarch/cli/render_hyprlock.py refuses to write a variable that is not listed here. Types follow hyprlock's own vocabulary: bool, int, float, string, color (rgb()/rgba()), gradient (one or more colors plus an optional angle), layoutxy (vec2, pixels or %). The manual is the only published specification; hyprlock has no JSON schema to validate against and no version tag was fetched, so 'verified_against' names the manual page rather than a release.
search_path_note: The first match wins, so the repo's .config/hypr/hyprlock.conf is what a session finds.

compositor_fade.note: Fades the lock surface's own opacity together with the compositor's blur contribution, using the fadeIn/fadeOut animations. Falls back to a client-side fade when the compositor does not advertise hyprland_surface_manager_v1. It animates the blur's contribution, not the blur radius.

disable_screencopy.note: Stops taking the screencopy used for background effects. Useful with a semitransparent background and Hyprland's misc:session_lock_xray enabled.

fail_timeout.note: Milliseconds until the UI resets after a failed authentication attempt.

fractional_scaling.enum_note: Documented inline in the general table; hyprlock has no named constant for it.

ignore_empty_input.note: Skips validation when no password was typed. Enabling it would let Enter on an empty field reach PAM, so this project never does.

immediate_render.note: Draw widgets immediately; backgrounds show background:color until their background:path resource is available.

screencopy_mode.note: 0 is GPU-accelerated, 1 is CPU-based and slow.
screencopy_mode.enum_note: Documented inline in the general table.

text_trim.note: Trims rendered text, to avoid trailing newlines in a command's output.

auth.note: At least one authentication method must be enabled. There is no key for a password file, a hash or an unlock command: hyprlock authenticates through PAM or fprintd and nothing else.

pam:module.note: The PAM module used for authentication; falls back to 'su' when it is not in /etc/pam.d. This project leaves it at the default rather than naming a module that may not exist on the reader's system.

fingerprint:enabled.note: Parallel fingerprint authentication through fprintd. Off unless the machine has a scanner and fprintd running; hyprlock reports the failure through the label substitutions $FPRINTPROMPT and $FPRINTFAIL.

fingerprint:retry_delay.note: Milliseconds after an unrecognized finger before another scan is accepted.

animations.note: hyprlock's animation keyword takes the same shape as Hyprland's (animation = NAME, ENABLED, DURATION_SECONDS, BEZIER), but the STYLE parameter is currently unused by hyprlock, and these durations are its own: they are not read from hyprland.lua and there is no global speed multiplier here.

bezier.note: bezier = NAME, X1, Y1, X2, Y2. Declared once per curve and referenced by name from the animation lines.

animation.note: animation = NAME, ENABLED, DURATION_SECONDS, BEZIER_NAME. The usable names come from hyprlock's own animation tree, recorded below.

animations.tree_note: fadeIn fades to the lock screen and fadeOut back to the session; the inputField names cover the colour and gradient transitions, the fade_on_empty animation, the adaptive-width animation and the individual dots. Naming an animation outside this tree does nothing.

positioning.note: Every widget takes monitor (empty = all monitors, or a Hyprland monitor reference such as eDP-1 or desc:...), position (an offset added to the result of alignment, in pixels or %), halign, valign and zindex (larger numbers draw on top; every widget defaults to 0 except background, which defaults to -1).

halign.enum_note: Documented under 'General Remarks'; no named constant.

valign.enum_note: Documented under 'General Remarks'; no named constant.

shadowable.note: Available on the widgets marked Shadowable: background, shape, input-field and label. shadow_passes = 0 disables the shadow entirely.

clickable.note: Available on label, image and shape only. The input field is *not* clickable, so nothing on a lock screen can be wired to a command by clicking it.

onclick.note: Arbitrary command run when the widget is clicked. This project emits none: a lock screen that runs a command on click is a lock screen with an unlock bypass one misclick away.

background.note: If path is empty or missing the widget fills with color; if path is the literal word screenshot, a capture of the desktop taken at launch is used. The blur options are Hyprland's own, so they take the same meaning -- and the same numbers -- as decoration:blur in hyprland.lua.

path.note: An image path, the word screenshot, or empty to fill with color. png, jpg and webp; no animations.

vibrancy.note: Saturation boost applied to blurred colours.

vibrancy_darkness.note: How strongly vibrancy affects dark areas. Hyprland's own blur has no equivalent leaf, so this one has no counterpart in data/design/tokens.json.

reload_time.note: Seconds between background reloads; 0 reloads on SIGUSR2. Ignored when path is screenshot.

reload_cmd.note: Command whose output becomes the new path; empty keeps the old one.

crossfade_time.note: Seconds of cross-fade between the old and new background on reload; a negative value means no cross-fade.

xray.note: Cuts a hole in the background: an unrotated rectangle of the shape's size.

input-field.note:
The password field. placeholder_text and fail_text both take the variable substitutions recorded below, and all rendered text takes pango markup (hyprlock also parses
as a line break).

outline_thickness.note: At 0 the inner box's colour changes instead of the outline's.

dots_center.note: Aligns the dots left when false.

dots_text_format.note: Characters used as the input indicator; rounded rectangles are the default.

hide_input.note: Renders a swaylock-style input indicator instead of dots.

hide_input_base_color.note: This colour's hue is rotated at random in oklab space to produce the hide_input colours, so a fixed palette cannot predict them.

rounding.note: -1 means complete rounding, i.e. a circle or oval.

check_color.note: Accent while waiting for the authentication result.

invert_numlock.note: Changes colour when Num Lock is off instead.

swap_font_color.note: Swaps the font and inner colours on colour-change events. With outline_thickness at 0 that means Caps Lock and the check state; otherwise the password check and an authentication failure. It also narrows a gradient accent to its first colour.

label.note: text takes variable substitution and, with the cmd[update:MILLISECONDS] prefix, runs a shell command on a timer. update:<time>:1 (or :true) also refreshes on SIGUSR2. A command that never exits hangs the AsyncResourceGatherer, so the only command this project emits is date. $TIME and $TIME12 use $TZ, then the system timezone, then UTC.

text_align.note: Multi-line alignment inside the label container: center, right, or any other value for the default left.

image.not_used_note: Recorded so a later change finds it verified instead of inventing it. This project ships no image widget: an avatar or logo on a lock screen is a path on somebody's disk that a generator cannot know, and the palette is already carried by the blurred desktop behind the field.

path.note: png, jpg or webp; no animations.

size.note: Both width and height; -1 keeps the aspect ratio.

reload_time.note: Seconds between reloads; 0 reloads on SIGUSR2.

substitutions.note: Available in widget text options. $ATTEMPTS[<string>] shows <string> only when there have been no failed attempts; $LAYOUT[a,b,c] replaces indexed keyboard layouts and a lone ! hides one. Variables are parsed *before* a cmd[] command runs.

keys_and_signals.locked_flag_note: Hyprland's `locked` bind flag lets a keybind work while hyprlock is active -- this repo already uses it for the volume, brightness and media keys in .config/hypr/keybind.lua.

signals.SIGUSR1: Unlocks hyprlock. `pkill -USR1 hyprlock` from another TTY therefore unlocks the session without a password. That is hyprlock's documented behaviour, not a misconfiguration, and it is why SECURITY.md cannot call the lock screen a boundary against a local user who can already run commands as you.

arch_linux_note: On Arch, hyprlock integrates with pambase through pam_faillock.so, which forces a 10 minute timeout after 3 failed unlocks. Changing that means editing /etc/security/faillock.conf (unlock_time, fail_interval, deny) -- a system file this project does not write.

not_in_hyprlock.note: Features this project's design brief asks for that hyprlock has no setting for, recorded so nobody invents a key that silently does nothing.

items.per-widget blur: Only background blurs. A frosted card behind the input field has to be a semi-transparent shape colour, not a blur.
items.radius token: rounding is an int in pixels (-1 for a circle); there is no percentage rounding and no shared radius scale.
items.global speed multiplier: Each animation line carries its own duration in seconds, so data/design/animations/*.json cannot be applied here directly -- only read for a duration.
items.theme or palette file: Colours are literals in this file, so the generator has to resolve the palette itself.
items.unlock command: Authentication is PAM or fprintd. There is no password file, no hash and no 'run this to unlock'.
items.idle timeout: hyprlock does not lock itself; an idle daemon does. See hypridle_fallback below.

hypridle_fallback.note: hypridle is Hyprland's idle daemon and refuses to run without a config file. This project ships one *unlaunched*: the shell already runs its own idle system (Noctalia's [idle.behavior.*], driven by ext_idle_notifier_v1 and respecting D-Bus and Wayland idle inhibitors), so starting a second daemon means two processes racing to lock, dim and suspend the same session. The file exists so a session with no shell has something to run; docs/glass-experience.md gives the one line that starts it.

lock_cmd.note: Runs on a D-Bus lock event, e.g. loginctl lock-session.

on_lock_cmd.note: Runs when a lock screen app locks the session.

before_sleep_cmd.note: Runs on the D-Bus prepare_sleep event.

inhibit_sleep.note: 0 disables sleep inhibition, 1 waits for before_sleep_cmd, 2 is auto, 3 waits for a lock screen app to lock the session.
inhibit_sleep.enum_note: Documented inline in the general table; no named constant.

timeout.note: Idle seconds. Must be specified; there is no default.

on-resume.note: Runs when activity is detected after on-timeout fired.

ignore_inhibit.note: Ignores idle inhibitors of every type for this listener.

condition_cmd.note: Run through /bin/sh -c when the timeout is reached, *before* on-timeout. Exit 0 lets on-timeout fire; non-zero defers it. Runs synchronously on hypridle's event loop, so it must be fast.

condition_retry.note: Re-runs condition_cmd every N seconds while the user stays idle, firing on-timeout as soon as it succeeds. 0 disables retrying and skips the deferred on-timeout for this idle cycle. Checked on hypridle's ~5 s tick, so smaller values are effectively rounded up.

hypridle_fallback.listeners_note: Any number of listener { } blocks may appear, in any order. This project's file declares none: with no listener, hypridle only runs the general commands, which is exactly the fallback role -- lock before sleep, and lock on a D-Bus lock event -- with no second set of idle timers to disagree with the shell's.

commands.note: The three command strings .config/hypr/hypridle.conf ships, recorded because two of them are shell syntax and one of them is Lua, and the hypridle manual alone does not show that. hypridle runs every command through /bin/sh -c (spawn(), hypridle src/core/Hypridle.cpp:286-289, the same at v0.1.8 and on main), which is what makes the || in lock_cmd and the quoting in after_sleep_cmd work at all; the six general:*_cmd values are plain Hyprlang STRINGs (hypridle src/config/ConfigManager.cpp:66-71). None of the three is built from user input, so there is no string to escape.

lock_cmd.note: Prefer the lock surface that is already running and only start a second one when it is not -- the same `pidof x || y` shape the hypridle manual's own example uses. The shell's lock screen reads ~/.config/noctalia/config.toml; hyprlock reads the hyprlock.conf next to this file.

before_sleep_cmd.note: Asks logind to lock the session, which the shell answers through ext_session_lock_v1 and hyprlock answers directly. Spelled this way in the hypridle manual's example.

after_sleep_cmd.note: The remedy for a display that needs a key press to come back after resume. The spelling is the compositor's rather than the daemon's: Hyprland v0.57.2 answers `hyprctl dispatch X` by evaluating `return hl.dispatch(X)` as Lua whenever the config provider is Lua (src/ipc/s1/Commands.cpp:1332-1350), and this session's config is Lua, so the legacy `dpms on` form reaches the Lua compiler as `hl.dispatch(dpms on)` and comes back a syntax error. hl.dsp.dpms is the dispatcher that exists (src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsDispatchers.cpp:1380, one argument, a table), and its action words are enable/on, disable/off and toggle, with anything else silently toggling instead of failing (LuaBindingsInternal.cpp:317-325, field name `action` at LuaBindingsInternal.hpp:151) -- which is why the word is spelled out here rather than left to a default. A successful dispatch replies `ok`, and hyprctl exits 7 only when the reply starts with `error:` (hyprctl/src/main.cpp:283-288), so the reply has to be read rather than merely waited for.
after_sleep_cmd.rejected_note: What the hypridle manual's after_sleep_cmd example uses and what this file shipped until the compositor's own dispatch path was read. It cannot work on a Lua-config Hyprland v0.57.2, for the reason in the note above. `hyprctl keyword` is no way round it either: no keyword command is registered anywhere at v0.57.2 (only a plugin may register one, src/plugins/PluginAPI.cpp:357), an unregistered request answers `unknown request` (src/ipc/s1/S1.cpp:107) and hyprctl still exits 0 because that reply does not start with `error:`, and the manual says outright that keyword 'will not work if your config provider is lua (refer to eval)' (docs/hyprctl.1.rst:36-40).
